Top anomaly

Polymarket's US–Iran peace deal by May 311 prints at 4%, down from 8% a week ago, and the Hormuz blockade-lifting contract fell from 33% to 18% in 48 hours. The market has, in effect, stopped pricing a deal. In the same window Ukraine's SBU destroyed two Tu-142 aircraft and an Iskander system at Taganrog2 and struck the Feodosiya oil terminal in Crimea; Russia retaliated with 290 drones and five Kh-101 cruise missiles.

What deserves attention is not the deadline itself but the shape of the response: fresh OFAC Counter-Terrorism Designations3 and an amended Iran FAQ suggest an administration hardening its floor to denuclearization rather than reaching for an exit.

Why it matters

Energy and escalation risk just repriced together — rare, and usually a leading indicator.

What's contested

The May 24 ceasefire was never formally extended — but never formally broken. The "rupture" read is an inference.
